intro: Friday brings steerable speech recognition, structured AI prompts and programmable security controls. BC housing figures and coastal storm totals lead local news, while Icelandic cooking, seasonal jazz and a December technology gathering offer dates to plan around.

stories.title: Salesforce releases steerable transcription
stories.summary: Salesforce introduced SOV-Transcribe-1, an Apache 2.0 speech model with four billion active parameters for non-streaming transcription. Developers can supply difficult vocabulary and control transcript formatting, giving specialized dictation and recorded-audio applications another open-weight option.

stories.title: Granite previews mark the boundary between instructions and data
stories.summary: IBM released experimental Granite 4.1 3B and 8B models trained on LLMON, a format that explicitly marks instructions, data and requirements. A companion toolkit lets developers test structured workflows and investigate resistance to indirect prompt injection.

stories.title: GitHub makes repository AI Scan settings programmable
stories.summary: GitHub’s public preview adds REST controls for enabling repository AI Scan across organizations and individual repositories. Administrators can automate rollout, but enabling the setting does not launch scans; users still run them on demand using Code Security AI credits.

stories.title: Secret scanning recognizes Cloudflare service tokens
stories.summary: GitHub added detection for Cloudflare Access service tokens in repositories, expanding its supported credential patterns. Teams using those tokens should review their secret-scanning alerts and investigate exposed credentials before continuing to rely on them.

stories.title: BC home sales fall almost 11%
stories.summary: BC recorded 5,670 home sales in October, almost 11% fewer than a year earlier, according to the provincial real estate association. Greater Vancouver sales fell 10%, while the province’s average sale price declined about 2.8%.

stories.title: Port Mellon records 307 millimetres of rain
stories.summary: Environment Canada’s overnight summary reports 307 millimetres at Port Mellon and 135 at Squamish Airport during storms beginning Tuesday morning. Horseshoe Bay received 80 millimetres, while West Vancouver recorded 66; the totals remain preliminary.
